mechaber.he: כמה דיני כתובה. ובו יג סעיפים: אסור להתייחד עם הכלה קודם שיכתוב לה כתובה (ויש מקילין ומתירין להתייחד בלא כתובה ובלבד שלא יבעול) (הר"ן ריש כתובות) והבעל נותן שכר הסופר ואפי' אם ירצה לייחד לה כתובתה במעות או בשאר מטלטלין אין שומעין לו אלא צריך שיכתוב לה שטר על עצמו בדמי הכתובה ויהיו כל נכסיו משועבדים לה או שיעידו עליו עדים ויקנו מידו שהוא חייב לה מנה או מאתים: הגה וי"א דאין לסמוך אעדים רק בשעת הדחק ומיד שיש לו פנאי לכתוב צריך לכתוב כ"ש שאין לסמוך עלייהו לכתחילה (כן משמע מלשון הטור וכ"כ מהרי"ק שורש ס"ד ומרדכי ריש כתובות) וכן ראוי להורות העמיד לה ערב קבלן בעד כתובתה והתנה שהוא יהא פטור ממנה אסור עד שיהא שעבודה עליו שלא תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה (ב"י בשם הרשב"א בתשו') וע' בחושן המשפט סי' ס' אם יוכל לשעבד עצמו בכתובתה בנכסים שלא באו לעולם ואין לעדים לחתום הכתובה אלא לאחר שקבל החתן קנין לפניהם (דברי הרב) ויש מקומות שמקילין בזה מרדכי פ"ב דגיטין וכן שיש עדים חותמים על הכתובות שקראו תחת החופה אע"פ שהם לא שמעו הקריאה אע"פ דלא שפיר עבדי אין לשנות מנהגן שלא להוציא לעז על כתובות הראשונות (אור זרוע):
mechaber.en: Laws of the ketubah. It contains 13 seifim. It is forbidden to be alone with the bride before he writes her a ketubah. {Rama: Some are lenient and permit being alone without a ketubah, provided he does not have intercourse (Ran beginning of Kesubos).} And the husband pays the scribe's fee. And even if he wishes to designate her ketubah in money or other movable property — we do not listen to him; rather he must write her a document upon himself for the ketubah amount and all his property shall be collateralized to her; or witnesses testify about him and acquire from him that he owes her a maneh or two hundred. {Rama: Some say one may rely on witnesses only in a time of duress, and as soon as he has leisure to write he must write — all the more so one may not rely on them ab initio (so implied from Tur's language, and likewise Maharik root 64 and Mordechai beginning of Kesubos); and so it is proper to rule. If he appointed a guarantor for her ketubah and stipulated that he would be exempt from it — it is forbidden until there is an obligation upon him so that divorcing her would not be light in his eyes (Beit Yosef in name of Rashba in a responsum). And see Choshen Mishpat siman 60 whether he can collateralize himself for her ketubah with property not yet in existence. Witnesses may not sign the ketubah until after the groom accepts kinyan before them (the master's words). And there are places that are lenient in this (Mordechai ch. 2 of Gittin). And likewise where witnesses sign on ketubot that were read under the chuppah even though they did not hear the reading — even though they do not act properly, one should not change their custom so as not to cast aspersion on earlier ketubot (Or Zarua).}

turei_zahav.he:

והבעל נותן שכר הסופר כמו בכל שט"ח שהלו' נותן שכר:
וי"א דאין לסמוך על עדים כולי הוא דעת הטור כ"כ בשם הרמב"ם והב"י חולק על כ' הטור בהבנת דברי הרמב"ם וז"ל הרמב"ם א' הכותב לבתול' כו' וא' שהעידו עליו עדים וקנו מידו שהוא חייב לה ק' או ר' ה"ז מותר וכן אם נתן לה מטלטלין נגד כתובתה ה"ז מותר לבעול עד שיהיה לו תנאי לכתוב עכ"ל כ' הטור אם שכח לייחד לה מטלטלין יבעול ואח"כ יכתוב לה מיד ואח"כ כ' בשם הרמב"ם בלשון זה וכן אם העיד עליו עדים וקנו ממנו שהוא חייב לה ה"ז מותר עד שיהיה לו פנאי לכתוב עכ"ל וכ' ב"י דלא דק רבינו במ"ש דלרמב"ם בעינן בקנו מידו עד שיהיה לו פנאי לכתוב דזה אינו דהרי השוו' הרמב"ם קנו מידו לכתוב לה כתוב' אלא דוקא במייחד מטלטלים כ"כ דתיכף שיהיה לו פנאי צריך לכתוב אבל בקנו מידו מותר אע"פ שיש לו פנאי אלא שבק לה למחר וליומא אוחרא וע"כ כתב כאן או שיעידו עליו עדים כולי ואני משתומם על זה דאנו רואים כוונת רבינו להשמ' שלא מבין דברי הרמב"ם כהבנת ב"י והוא נכון דודאי קשה האיך נאמ' דבעדים וקנין א"צ להיות תיכף שיהיה לו פנאי דלמא נחלק בכך דהא עכ"פ צריך כתיבה דאע"ג דסתם קנין לכתיב עומד מ"מ הוא צריך לכתוב דלא סמכ' דעת' דשמא ימותו העדים או ירחקו נדוד מכאן ובמה יודע שהיה לה כתוב' ומטעם זה הצריך גם ב"י שיכתוב למחר וא"כ שיש צורך בכתיב' אח"כ ודאי דינו כשיהיה לו פנאי כמו במטלטלים שנקט אח"כ דלמא נחלק ביניהם בחילוק כזה בענין הפנאי כיון דהכרח הוא בשניהן ולא עוד אלא ק"ו הוא ממטלטלין דהא במטלטלים יש עכ"פ בידה הסך שלה אלא שיש חשש שמא יהיה נאבדים ע"כ צריך לכתוב ולשעבד נכסיו ק"ו בזה שאין ביד' כלום אלא סומכ' על קנין של עדים וכי עדים תמיד אצל' וסוף אדם למות לבעול והוא מוכח הגמרא דאמרינן דשרי לבעל כשמתפיס לה מטלטלין ולא אמר עד שיקנו מידו א"ו דלא מהני בזדה עדים וקני אלא דוקא אם (הוא) קודם החופה בשע' שכותבין הכתיבה מהני ההוא שעתא אם קנו אע"פ שלא נכתב עדיין ענין כמו שכותב כתובה שהיא קודם חופה משא"כ בבא דמטלטלין מיירי אפילו אחר החופה דהיינו קודם הבעילה וכונ' זו מתבארת היטב בלשון הרמב"ם שכ' בזה ה"ז מותר לבעול ובבא ראשונה כ' ה"ז מותר ולא זכר לבעול אלא ברור מבואר בל' רבינו הטור שכ' תחלה דבשכח לכותבם יכול לייחד מטלטלים כדי שיבעול ויכתוב לה מיד אח"כ ואח"כ ביאר הדבר מה נקרא מיד אח"כ דודאי לא נימא תכף אחר שיבעול אלא היינו או שיהיה לו פנאי וע"ז מביא דברי תחילה מטעם שזכרתי דכאן בקנו בעדים מיירי קודם החופ': וצריך שתדע דבמה שזכר הרמב"ם אחר שהעידו עליו עדים אין פירושו שיבואו העדים לב"ד ויעידו כן דלאו ברשיעי עסקינן דנחשד לשקר אלא דעיקר ההיתר קמ"ל שאסור' לו עד שיעידו עדים וקנו ואם הוא עשה כן מותרת לו אעפ"י שלא נכתב עדיין אלא בועל ויכתוב כשיהיה פנאי אח"כ וזה מבואר בפירו' בלשון הטור שכ' וכן אם העיד עליו עדים כו' היינו שהוא עשה כן אז מותרת לו כ"ז הוא ברור ונכון בס"ד ויפ' דק רבינו הטור בדבריו אלה ויהא רעוא דיהוי נהירין לנו בכל דוכתא כהא מלתא בס"ד:

(א) ' behold to divorce' wrote Beit Yosef in name of Rashi there is no ketubah collect ketubah even wrote if beit din therefore to remain wife ketubah.
(ב) husband scribe's fee like " '.
(ג) And some say that one may not rely on witnesses, etc. This is the Tur's view, which he wrote in the name of Rambam. Beit Yosef disputes what the Tur wrote in understanding Rambam's words. Rambam wrote: whether one writes for a virgin, etc., or witnesses testified about him and made a kinyan from him that he owes her one hundred or two hundred, this is permitted; and likewise if he gave her movable property corresponding to her ketubah, it is permitted for him to have relations until he has time to write. End quote. The Tur wrote: if he forgot to designate movable property for her, he may have relations and afterward write for her immediately. Afterward he wrote in Rambam's name in this language: likewise if witnesses testified about him and made a kinyan from him that he owes her, this is permitted until he has time to write. Beit Yosef wrote that our teacher was not exact in writing that according to Rambam, where they made a kinyan from him, we require only until he has time to write; this is not so, for Rambam equated making a kinyan from him with writing her a ketubah. Rather, specifically when he designates movable property, as soon as he has time he must write; but with a kinyan, it is permitted even if he has time, and he may leave it until tomorrow or another day. Therefore the Mechaber wrote here, "or witnesses testify about him," etc. I am astonished at this, for we see that the Tur intended to teach that he did not understand Rambam like Beit Yosef did, and this is correct. It is certainly difficult to say that with witnesses and a kinyan he need not write as soon as he has time. Why distinguish? In any case writing is required. Although an ordinary kinyan stands for writing, nevertheless he must write, for her mind does not rely on it, lest the witnesses die or travel far away, and by what will it be known that she had a ketubah? For this reason Beit Yosef also required writing the next day. Since there is a need for later writing, certainly its law is that he must write when he has time, as with movable property. All the more so from movable property: with movable property at least she has her sum in hand, and the concern is only lest it be lost, so he must write and encumber his property; here she has nothing in hand and relies only on the kinyan of witnesses. Are witnesses always with her? Ultimately people die. Certainly she needs a written ketubah more, and therefore it must be written as soon as he has time. It is therefore clear that Rambam's final phrase "until he has time" applies also to witnesses and kinyan.

pitchei_teshuva.en: Only in a time of duress. See Ba'er Hetev and Yeshuot Yaakov s.k. 2, who elaborated and concluded to distinguish: if at the time he accepted kinyan he had leisure to write and the woman could have asked the witnesses to write for her — for we hold "they acquired from him" needs no further consultation — the kinyan helps even not in duress, per Beit Yosef's view; and even if she did not go ask the witnesses, she herself is proof she relied, so kinyan helps like writing even without duress. But if at that time he could not write — such as Shabbat or no leisure — we say she did not rely on kinyan and it helps only like seizing movable property, which helps only in duress. See there.

mechaber.he: אם כתב לה כתובה ונאבדה או שמחלה לו (ודוקא) שכתבה לו התקבלתי כתובתי צריך לכתוב אחרת בעיקר הכתובה שאסור לאדם לשהות עם אשתו שעה אחת בלא כתובה: הגה עיר שכבשוהו כרכום או שגלו מן העיר ואבדו הנשים הכתובות שלהם צריכים לחדש נשותיהם כתובתיהם אע"פ שיש לומר שמא ימצאו אח"כ כתובותיהם או יחזרו להם מ"מ מאחר שהכתובות בחזקת אבודות צריכין כתובות אחרות ואם אינו ידוע סך הכתובות אם ישארו קצתן אזלינן בתרייהו ואם לאו דנין על פי זקני העיר ולפי המנהג העשיר לפי עשרו והעני לפי עניו (ב"י בשם תשובות הגאונים) וכשנאבדה הכתובה ובא לכתוב לה כתובה אחרת צריך לכתוב לה כתובה גדולה כראשונה (מהרי"ק שורש קט"ז) וע' לקמן סי' קע"ז דבמקום שאין מגרשין רק מרצון האשה א"צ לכתוב כתובה א"כ בזמן הזה במדינות אלו שאין מגרשין בעל כרחה של אשה משום חרם ר"ג וכמו שיתבאר לקמן סי' קי"ט היה אפשר להקל בכתיבת הכתובה אבל אין המנהג כן ואין לשנות (כל זה ד"ע):
mechaber.en:
If he wrote her a ketubah and it was lost, or she waived it to him — specifically if she wrote him "I received my ketubah" — he must write another for the principal ketubah, for it is forbidden for a man to remain with his wife even one hour without a ketubah.

{Rama: A city that was conquered or from which they were exiled and the women's ketubot were lost — they must renew their wives' ketubot, even though one might say perhaps their ketubot will later be found or returned to them; nevertheless, since the ketubot are presumed lost, other ketubot are required. And if the sum of the ketubot is unknown — if some will remain, we follow both of them; and if not, we judge according to the elders of the city and according to custom — the rich according to his wealth and the poor according to his poverty (Beit Yosef in name of responsa of the Geonim). And when the ketubah was lost and he comes to write her another ketubah — he must write her a ketubah as large as the first (Maharik root 116). And see below siman 177 that in a place where they divorce only with the woman's consent, a ketubah need not be written; if so, nowadays in these countries where a man does not divorce a woman against her will because of Rabbenu Gershom's ban, as will be explained below siman 119 — one could be lenient in writing the ketubah; but the custom is not so and one should not change (all this is the master's view).}

beit_shmuel.en:
(א) Specifically where she wrote to him, "I have received." This implies that if she waives orally, he need not write her another ketubah, and there is no prohibition in living with her without a ketubah. At first glance this is astonishing, for there is still concern that she does not rely on the waiver and thinks the waiver is effective; if so, the relations would be like promiscuous relations, as written by the Rosh and Tosafot. One must say that when she waives orally we are not concerned for this. Tosafot and the Rosh speak of a stipulation at the time of kiddushin, where she thinks the condition stands; but with an oral waiver afterward, she does not think the waiver stands. So wrote Bach. However, one can also say that even orally she does not rely on it; rather, orally there is a remedy without another ketubah, namely to tell her that the waiver is ineffective. But when she wrote "I have received," the lien of the ketubah is cancelled and he must write her another ketubah. Yet below it is proven that the Mechaber holds primarily like Rambam, that even writing is ineffective and she does not lose the ketubah. If so, the requirement to write her a ketubah must be because her mind does not rely on it; and when she waives orally, he need not write another ketubah. Therefore one must say that her mind does rely on it when she waives orally. The Rav Rama's word "specifically" is learned from Mordekhai in chapter HaChovel, who wrote on the statement "with respect to a husband she certainly waives" that this is specifically where she wrote "I have received"; but mere waiver is not a waiver once she is already married. Chelkat Mechokek wrote that although Maggid Mishneh ruled regarding a debt document that waiver is effective even if the document is still held, one can distinguish: with a ketubah, for a woman sitting under her husband, as long as she has not written "I have received," she can say, "I was joking with you and spoke empty words." After her husband's death, however, Maggid Mishneh's words imply that even with a ketubah, mere waiver is effective. Thus from Mordekhai we hear that when she writes "I have received," she has no ketubah, unlike Rambam, who holds that even if she wrote "I have received" she still has a ketubah. The Mechaber follows Rambam.

pitchei_teshuva.en: As large as the first. See responsum Motzal Me'esh siman 25: a woman whose ketubah document was lost and her husband wrote another — the first was ten thousand, the second five thousand, and she did not protest. If the first is later found and she is divorced or widowed — is the first obligation waived, or since she thought it lost but now it is found the first debt still stands? He answered: if the second ketubah does not mention nedunya or addition but plainly writes five thousand because the Sages forbade remaining without ketubah — if the first is later found, the obligation was never waived; only the maneh or two hundred principal was waived, and he wrote the second only for the prohibition, which is only maneh and two hundred. But nedunya and other matters that are a full loan were not waived by writing another ketubah for maneh and two hundred; and the five thousand written — even if maneh and two hundred sufficed — we say he added as Rama wrote. Even if the first is never found, if there is no contradiction and the husband claims the second ketubah waived the first — that is not in his power. But if the new ketubah mentions nedunya and addition and she knew and accepted — certainly the first ketubah is void, even if only a shard is found. So he ruled.

(ועיין בתשי' חתם סופר ס"ס קל"ג שכ' וז"ל ולענין כתוב' דנושא מפותת עצמו הייתי נוהג לכתוב מאתים ע"פ ל' הטור סי' קע"ז עד שמצאתי בס' דגמ"ר שכ' דהיינו בנער' אבל לא בבוגרת דאין לה אלא מנה וכבר הורה זקן וכן ראוי עכ"ל. ושם בסי' קכ"ה אודות אחת שילדה אחר החתונ' בקרוב והוא והיא מודים שממנו נתעברה באופן שאין ספק משום מינקת חבירו ונתעורר רב ח' על שנכתב בכתוב' מאתים כבתול' ובס' דגמ"ר כתב דאם היא בוגרת אין לה אלא מנה (וא"כ אפסר הכתוב' פסולה) והוא ז"ל השיב אמת נכון הדבר אע"ג דתנן ר"פ אע"פ שאם רצה להוסיף מוסיף ודעת הר"ן שם שיכול לכלול התוספות בסכום א' עם הכתובה בסתם ולא כמרדכי מ"מ מודה הר"ן דלא מצי למכתב דחזי ליכי מדאורייתא כו' וגם הא ודאי שדברי דגמ"ר הנ"ל נכונים מאד דבוגרת שאין לה קנס ובשגם כי בעילה ראשונה מחלה מדעתה גם הרמב"ם מודה דאין לה אלא מנה ומ"מ בנ"ד אין שום חשש דנ"ל דכל זה במפתה בוגרת דעלמא ונשאה אח"כ אבל במשודכת שלו וכבר נכתב ביניהם תנאים בחרם וקנס כנהוג שלבה סמוך ובטוח שתנשא לו ואדעת' דהכי אפקרה נפשה לגבי דידיה שהוא ישאנה ויהיה כתובתה ממנו מאתים כמוהר הבתולות בודאי לא מחלה אלא אדעתא דהכי כו' ואפי' אם יתעקש אדם לומר שאם הבועל הזה אינו רוצה לכתו' מאתים לא נוכל לכופו אבל עכ"פ אם כתב לה מאתים דחזי ליכי איך ניקום ונא' דלא חזי לה ממנו כי בודאי חזי וראוי ומחוייב לכתוב כן עכ"ד ע"ש) ומ"ש הבה"ט בשם הר"ם מינץ מי שאנס בתולה ונשא' לו כו' עמ"ש לקמן סי' קמ"ג סק"ו ביאור דברי הר"ם מינץ בזה:
pitchei_teshuva.en: And for a widow a maneh. Dagul MeRevavah wrote: the questioner asks how much is a seduced woman's ketubah — see Tur siman 177, Rambam ch. 1 Laws of Na'arah halakhah 3, and Maggid Mishneh there; and it seems all this when she was a minor, but an adult who was seduced — certainly even per Rambam and Tur she has only a maneh even if the seducer himself marries her. These matters are stated at length in Noda B'Yehuda second edition siman 33; see there and below siman 177 s.k. 3. See also Chasam Sofer end of siman 133: regarding one who marries his own seduced woman I would write two hundred per Tur siman 177 until I found in Dagul MeRevavah that this applies only to a minor, not an adult who has only a maneh — the elder so ruled and so is proper. And there siman 125 regarding one who conceived soon after the wedding and they admit the pregnancy is from him without doubt of another man's nursing — a sage challenged that two hundred was written as for a virgin, and Dagul MeRevavah wrote that if she is an adult she has only a maneh (and thus the ketubah is invalid); he answered it is correct, even though we learn "if he wishes to add he may add" and Ran holds additions may be included in one sum with the ketubah plainly, not like Mordechai — nevertheless Ran agrees one cannot write "that which is fitting for you from the Torah," and Dagul MeRevavah's words are very correct for an adult who has no fine and whose first intercourse was with consent — Rambam also agrees she has only a maneh. Nevertheless in our case there is no concern, for all this is a generally seduced adult who later marries; but for his betrothed with conditions and penalties as customary, her heart was confident she would marry him and knowingly gave herself to him that he would marry her with two hundred like virgin bride-price — certainly she waived only with this understanding. And even if one stubbornly says if this seducer will not write two hundred we cannot compel him — at minimum if he wrote two hundred "that which is fitting for you," how can we say it is not fitting from him, for certainly it is fitting and he is obligated to write so. See there. And what Ba'er Hetev cited from R' Meir Mintz regarding one who raped a virgin and married her — see below siman 143 s.k. 6 for explanation of R' Meir Mintz's words.

mechaber.he: כמה שיעור הכתובה לבתולה ק"ק ולאלמנה מנה ושל זו וזו כסף מדינה נמצא כתובות בתולה הם ל"ז דרהם וחצי כסף צרוף וכתובת אלמנה מחציתם שהם י"ח דרהם וג' רביעים כסף צרוף: הגה ע' בי"ד סי' רצ"ד וסי' ש"ה ערך המטבע שנקראת דרהם וכ"ז לדעת קצת הפוסקים שסבירא להו שכתובת בתולה אינה רק זוזי דרבנן (הרי"ף והרמב"ם והר"ן והר"ם) שמאתים של בתולה עולין ששה סלעים ורביע ויש מי שמשער כתובת בתולה י' זהובים ואלמנה חמשה זהובים (מהרי"ל בשם אגודה) אבל לדעת יש פוסקים מאתים של בתולה ומנה של אלמנה משערים בזוזי דאורייתא והוא ח' פעמים יותר וכתבו דלכן נהגו לכתוב בכתובה דחזי ליכי מדאורייתא (ר"ת) וי"א דכותבין דחזי לכי סתמא (הגהות מיי' פ"י דאישות) והמנהג לכתוב לבתולה דחזי ליכי מדאורייתא אבל לא לאלמנה וכ"ז במקום שאין מנהג אבל במקום שיש מנהג מה שגובין הולכין אחר המנהג וכמו שיתבאר לקמן:
mechaber.en:
What is the measure of the ketubah? For a virgin — two hundred; and for a widow — a maneh. And for both, provincial silver — thus a virgin's ketubah is 37.5 drachma of pure silver, and a widow's ketubah is half of that, which is 18.75 drachma of pure silver.

{Rama: See Yoreh Deah siman 294 and siman 305 for the value of the coin called drachma. And all this is per the view of some poskim who hold that a virgin's ketubah is only rabbinic zuzim (Rif, Rambam, Ran, and R' Meir of Rothenburg) — that two hundred for a virgin equals six and a quarter selaim. And some estimate a virgin's ketubah at ten gold coins and a widow's at five gold coins (Maharil in name of Agudah). But per the view of poskim, two hundred for a virgin and a maneh for a widow are estimated in Torah zuzim, which is eight times more; and they wrote that therefore the custom is to write in the ketubah "that which is fitting for you from the Torah" (Rabbeinu Tam). And some say they write "that which is fitting for you" plainly (Hagahot Maimoniyot ch. 10 of Ishut). The custom is to write for a virgin "that which is fitting for you from the Torah," but not for a widow — all this where there is no custom; but where there is custom, they follow what is collected according to custom, as will be explained below.}

Fixed Torah silver is Tyrian silver, while rabbinic silver is provincial silver, meaning one-eighth of Tyrian silver; this totals six and a quarter Tyrian selaim according to those poskim who hold that she collects provincial silver. (ג) In Torah zuzim. This implies that the ketubah is rabbinic, but we assess it in Torah zuzim. So it is according to the approach of all the poskim who hold that the ketubah of a virgin is rabbinic, and so ruled Beit Yosef and Darkei Moshe. Only Rabbenu Tam and Ri hold that a virgin's ketubah is Torah law. As for the formula "that is fit for you from the Torah," the Rosh wrote that it refers to Tyrian coinage, which is Torah coinage; the Sages enacted for her Torah-level coinage. At first glance, one must say so, for the Talmud states that according to the view that ketubah is Torah law, he is not believed to say "I found an open opening," as Mordekhai and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote; yet we rule that he is believed to say "I found an open opening." Necessarily, then, the formula "fit for you from the Torah" refers only to the coinage, unlike Perishah, who wrote that the ketubah is Torah law. His question, that if it refers to coinage why do we not write so for a widow, is not difficult. For a widow the Sages did not enact Tyrian silver; even according to Rabbenu Tam and Ri, who hold that a virgin's ketubah is Torah law, a widow's ketubah is rabbinic, as stated on Ketubot 10. According to the Rosh as well, the Sages did not enact Torah coinage for a widow. Hagahot Maimoniyot at the end of Ketubot, who holds that for a widow too they enacted Tyrian coinage, is a lone view. The gloss's statement that for a widow we assess in Torah zuzim follows Hagahot Maimoniyot, but the custom is not like him. Rather, the main law follows the general body of poskim: for a widow we do not assess in Torah zuzim. Even according to the custom that a widow collects half the amount of a virgin, it is still not appropriate to write "fit for you from the Torah," for the Sages did not enact that. Bach wrote that according to the view that ketubah is Torah law, one collects from intermediate-quality property. This does not appear to me, for Tosafot wrote that even according to R. בתכשיטין פרטים אבנים טובות ומרגליות אבל לא נזכר תכשיט כסף וזהב ובאחרונה הזכיר ותכשיטין כסף וזהב ואבנים טובות כו' וכיון שהזכיר פרטים שלא הכניס' כלל ש"מ שכוונתו על השייך לגופה גם מה שיעשה ויקנה לה אחר החתונה ומכל מקום מסיק דטוב לעשות פשר ע"ש ועיין מה שכתב לקמן סי צ"ט סק"א בשם גבעת שאול:
pitchei_teshuva.en: And writes more. Ba'er Hetev cited Beit Shmuel s.k. 23 through "and he can profit from them" from Beit Shmuel's language. Sefer HaPela'ah wrote in Kuntres Acharon letter 13: Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote this is not interest because even if he divorces or dies immediately he must give this addition. But per our enactments, in the first and second year he does not give the addition in full until after three years — thus this answer does not apply. See there where he elaborated; see also Hagahot Yad Efraim and in my view no need to elaborate per what is explained above siman 53 in Beit Shmuel s.k. 16 that returning within three years does not apply to nedunya law or one-third addition which is like a nedunya debt and she loses only regarding maneh and two hundred or voluntary addition. In my view these do not suffice to answer the aforementioned Gaon: first, Beit Shmuel's law that one-third addition is like nedunya is not agreed, for in our case it is clear she takes only nedunya not one-third addition as I brought there in his name. Further, Noda B'Yehuda second edition siman 12 wrote if he did not profit on the principal sum Beit Shmuel also agrees — brought there too. Further, the Gaon did not refer to ShUM enactment but another enactment, since he says "only after three years" while ShUM is only the second year; Yad Efraim there also cites "only after three years." Even if "after three" is a mistake for "after two," his language implies an enactment not to give the addition in full, like the custom now in the country I mentioned siman 53 s.k. 14 or Prague custom in responsum Eliyahu Zuta part 2 siman 147 giving half addition — the above answer does not apply. Nevertheless in my view I do not understand Sefer HaPela'ah's difficulty, for all these enactments whether ShUM or ours were enacted lest she remain empty — which applies only to death not divorce, for he divorces willingly; thus Hagahot Maimoniyot properly said it is not interest since even if he divorced immediately he must give this addition — it is not "waiting for payment," and "or if he dies" is incidental, but the main answer is if he divorces her. In Hagahot Ashri ch. Found Object of a Woman siman 4, R' Shmuel explained it is not interest since if he divorced immediately he would have to add; also Turei Zahav on that chapter brought this answer in Mordechai's name; also Beit Shmuel s.k. 16 brought this answer because if he divorces even immediately, etc. — and from omitting "or dies immediately" it appears they intended this; uncertain. See Brit Avraham siman 75 letter 1 who elaborated on Hagahot Ashri's main reason that even if he divorced immediately he must add — he proved in his work Hovat Chen siman 177 that even then it is interest, but concluded per Sefer Halakhot Ketanot it is not interest since perhaps collection will never come, like acquiring her property on doubt that if she dies he inherits, etc. See there. And what Ba'er Hetev further wrote about Krakow custom excluding garments, etc. — see Noda B'Yehuda second edition siman 100 questioned a ketubah stating the groom added one-third of the principal beyond garments and jewelry, doubting whether "belonging to her person" means the husband acquires for her or only what she brought; also that extra language was not used for jewelry as gift but only that she takes jewelry; he answered the necessity that it refers to what she brought is no proof, for there is relevance to two returns siman 53 and moredet siman 77 and taking without oath end of siman 88. On the contrary, it proves the intention is on what the husband does; if on what she brought, why write she takes all this besides ketubah — she would take nedunya besides ketubah even without writing. Beit Yosef Choshen Mishpat end of siman 61 in Rashba's name: we do not interpret extra language for benefit except where they said we have no power to judge imaginings; but siman 42 Beit Yosef brought Maharik who does interpret extra language; and Rashba did not close us off except where the matter itself must be written with only extra language, but where it need not be written at all we say from explicit writing it comes for benefit she would not otherwise deserve (he elaborated; apparently disputed between Tanna Kamma and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel Bava Metzia 83 — per our ruling like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, see Tur Choshen Mishpat siman 231 and Sma there; uncertain. See Bava Batra 67 and 138 and Perishah Choshen Mishpat siman 42 letter 10 where I elaborated). Thus also here the condition she takes applies to her person if the intention is nedunya she brought — entirely superfluous; though one may doubt why he wrote one-third addition for belongings she brought — it is strained; Beit Yosef Choshen Mishpat siman 42: whatever meaning is clear to beit din from the writing, they judge even for the husband's benefit, etc. Regarding the second doubt since he did not mention he added, etc. — in my youth I wondered why they give a widow per ketubah all belonging to her person even what the husband did not have at marriage — by what right, even if written as gift he did not obligate himself to buy jewelry, and post-wedding jewelry is not in his power to give as gift per Choshen Mishpat siman 259. I then justified the custom: since for a widow they assess what is upon her below siman 99 because she did not intend gift when leaving — we can say this is plainly, but where he wrote in the ketubah she takes all belonging to her person, he revealed he is pleased even when leaving she should take; thus when he gives after the wedding he acquires for her and she takes, not by kinyan at marriage. Therefore even inferior language not of gift, he revealed he wants her to take when leaving. Another reason for the custom: per Choshen Mishpat siman 259 s.k. 4 if he seized after it came into existence, etc. — specifically with effective language; thus one may doubt this ketubah. But we need my youth's reason, for if she acquires when it comes into existence — fine per Sma siman 66 s.k. 46 even seizure not before seller; but per Shach only when seller knows, and waiver applies to selling to a stranger, etc. — here if this woman acquires belongings it depends on Sma-Shach dispute; even per Sma my reason alone is straight; therefore hard to completely deny this woman belongings, better to favor the widow. See there siman 101 for further merit that jewelry specifics were listed initially but silver and gold jewelry were added finally — intention is on belongings he will acquire after the wedding; nevertheless he concludes compromise is good. See what he wrote below siman 99 s.k. 1 in name of Givat Shaul.

mechaber.he: אם ירצה להוסיף ע"ז מוסיף וזה התוספות שמוסיף יש דברים שדינו בהם כעיקר הכתובה ויש דברים שהוא חלוק בהם מעיקר הכתובה כדלקמן: הגה וא"צ לפרש עיקר הכתובה בפני עצמה והתוספת בפני עצמו אלא כולל הכל ביחד אם ירצה (הר"ן ריש אע"פ והמ"מ פ"י וריב"ש סי' ס"ח) וי"ח וסבירא להו דצריך לכתוב הכתובה כמנהג המדינה בפני עצמה והתוספת בפני עצמו וכן נוהגין ואם יש משפחה שכולן נוהגים בתוספת א"צ לכתוב כל א' בפני עצמו (מרדכי פ"ק דכתובות) כתובה שכתב בה ודין נדוניא דהנעלת ליה מאה דינרין והוסיף לה מן דיליה כך וכך אין עיקר כתובה בכלל וצריך לשלם לה בפני עצמו עד שיהיו כתוב ויהיבנא ליכי מוהר בתוליכי כסף זוזי אלף דאז העיקר כתובה בכלל (ריב"ש סי' ס"ה):
mechaber.en:
If he wishes to add to this — he may add. And this addition that he adds — some matters have the same law as the principal ketubah, and some matters are distinguished from the principal ketubah, as below.

{Rama: He need not specify the principal ketubah separately and the addition separately; rather he may include everything together if he wishes (Ran beginning of Even HaEzer and Maggid Mishneh ch. 10 and Rivash siman 68). And some dispute and hold that he must write the ketubah according to provincial custom separately and the addition separately — and so is the practice. And if there is a family where all practice with an addition — he need not write each one separately (Mordechai ch. 1 of Kesubos). A ketubah in which he wrote "and the nedunya that you brought him one hundred dinar and he added to her from his own such-and-such" — the principal ketubah is not included and he must pay her separately until it says "written and I give you your virgin bride-price, one thousand silver zuz" — then the principal ketubah is included (Rivash siman 65).}

pitchei_teshuva.en: They write "the divorced woman." Ba'er Hetev. See Chasam Sofer siman 130 regarding a divorcee's ketubah without "divorced woman": a rabbi went abroad for a month and it was hidden from everyone that Tashbetz part 2 siman 173 wrote they did not practice like Rambam (ch. 4 Laws of Yibum halakhah 33) to write in a divorcee's ketubah "so-and-so the divorcee," etc. He answered this is incorrect — if Tashbetz were before us he would require another ketubah or seizing movable property and writing another ketubah after chuppah, for one examining Tashbetz sees his main reason that one marrying her (if he checks this ketubah and sees she has only a maneh) knows she is a divorcee from the first, for if a widow she would be a killer and forbidden to all, etc. — meaning Rambam per his view is not concerned for killer-wife suspicion but only a mere concern, therefore concerned for priesthood; but per all poskim who are concerned for killer-wife, she has both priesthood and killer concerns, so how blame the woman on her husband. Therefore for us who are very lenient in the manners mentioned siman 9 in the gloss, the concern returns — thus great necessity to mention "divorced woman." And reciprocally, since they already practice as Rama wrote to write "divorced woman," even if Tashbetz himself were before us he would fear if this ketubah comes before a third party he would judge she is certainly not a divorcee since they practice writing "divorced woman" — thus what was done in the case before us is improper, etc. It would seem right to say the ketubah is invalid, not written for this divorcee woman but for a widow — she is another. But Maharam siman 109 wrote nevertheless it is not invalid, for a divorcee is also called a widow, etc., and I say because the Sages called widow after maneh — whoever collects a maneh can be called widow unless "widow" is written (and what he wrote above requiring another ketubah and even without writing widow — when he sensed the mistake before chuppah, as ab initio). See there. And what he wrote "if she had intercourse they write 'had intercourse.'" See Nishmat Adam not to write "had intercourse," so Beit Meir; write only "so-and-so betrothed" and that suffices as a sign. See responsum Radbaz part 1 siman 180: a convert married in ancient days, divorced, now remarries — do they write "the convert" or "the divorcee"? He answered apparently no concern since both are forbidden to priesthood; but on examination it is proper to write "the convert" so conversion is not forgotten, lest tomorrow this one divorces her and she marries a convert and his daughter is unfit for high priesthood per Ra'avad (ab initio when consulting they so instruct, see Kiddushin 48b and Maggid Mishneh siman 7 s.k. 21). Further relevance for marrying her father's relatives — they did not decree on a convert regarding father's relatives at all, and even mother's relatives there is relevance since prohibition is only rabbinic; therefore always write "the convert" so her lineage is not forgotten. Need not write "divorcee" for divorcee and widow are included in convert forbidden to priesthood. And for divorcee and widow write "the divorcee," etc. See there.

mechaber.he: הנושא אשה סתם כותב לפי המנהג וכן היא שפסקה להכניס נותנת כפי מנהג המדינה: הגה ומה שהאשה מכנסת לבעלה הן מעות הן בגדים ומקבלן עליו והן באחריותו נקרא נדוניא בכל מקום ואינה נגבית אלא עם הכתובה אבל לשאר דברים אין דינו ככתובה וכמו שיתבאר לקמן ויש מקומות שהחתן מוסיף לה בנדונייתא וכותב יותר ממה שקבל והולכין בזה אחר המנהג (כל הנ"ל בטור) ומן הסתם אחריות הנדוניא עליו כנכסי צאן ברזל אבל אם ירצה להניח לה ברשותה ושלא לקבל אחריות עליהם הרשות בידו וע"ל ריש סי' צ"ג וק' עוד מאלו הדינים כשהאב קיים ומשיא בתו כותבים ודין הנדוניא דהנעלת ליה מבי אביה וכשאין האב קיים כותבים מבי נשא (מרדכי פרק ב"מ בשם ר"ת) מיהו אם שינה לית לן בה (תשו' ר"ש משנ"ץ) בכתובות גרושה כותבין מתרכתא כדי שידעו שהיא גרושה ואסורה לכהנים (מפסקי מהרא"י סי' נ') וכשבאה לגבות כתובתה מגבין לה מה שבכתובתה לפי מנהג המדינה: הגה ואם היא אומרת שהוסיף לה יותר מן המנהג צריכה להביא ראייה לדבריה אבל אם יש בידה שטר כתובה שאינה מקוים או שא' מן העדים פסול אע"פ שמראה התנאים שביניהם שהוצרך להוסיף לה אינה גובאת אלא כמנהג (פסקי מהרא"י סי' פ"ט) וע"ל סי' ק' סעיף ל') ובכל אלו הדברים וכיוצא בהן מנהג המדינה הוא עיקר ועל פיו דנין והוא שיהיה אותו המנהג פשוט בכל המדינה: הגה מיהו אם רוצה להתנות ולפחות לאשתו מן המנהג הרשות בידו (מהרי"ל סי' ע"ו) ובלבד שלא יפחות ממה שתקנו רבנן ונ"ל דוקא שהתנה כן בשעה שעשה השידוכים אבל אם עשו שידוכים סתם ושעבדו עצמן בקנסות צריך לכתוב לפי המנהג ולא יוכל לשנות (דברי הרב וכן משמע במהרי"ל) ויש מקומות שנוהגים לכתוב כל הכתובות בשוה אפילו לא הכניסה לו כלום ואם ירצה מוסיף לה ואם ירצה לפחות לה היא כותבת לו כך וכך קבלתי על כתובתי וכן נוהגין במדינות אלו:
mechaber.en:
One who marries a woman without specification writes according to custom; and likewise she who undertook to bring a dowry gives according to provincial custom.

{Rama: And what the woman brings to her husband — whether money or garments — and he accepts them upon himself and they are under his responsibility — is called nedunya everywhere, and it is collected only with the ketubah; but for other matters its law is not like the ketubah, as will be explained below. And there are places where the groom adds to her in the nedunya and writes more than he received, and they follow custom in this (all the above in Tur). And by default responsibility for the nedunya is upon him like iron-flock property; but if he wishes to leave them in her possession and not accept responsibility for them — the choice is his. And see above beginning of siman 93 and 100 for more of these laws. When the father is alive and marries off his daughter they write "and the nedunya that you brought him from her father's house"; and when the father is not alive they write "from the house of the groom" (Mordechai ch. Bava Metzia in name of Rabbeinu Tam). However, if he changed the wording — we pay no attention (responsum of R' Shmuel of Nantes). For a divorcee's ketubah they write "the divorced woman" so they know she is a divorcee and forbidden to kohanim (Piskei Maharai siman 50). And when she comes to collect her ketubah — they collect for her what is in the ketubah according to provincial custom.

{Rama: And if she says he added more than the custom — she must bring proof for her claim. But if she has a ketubah document that is not validated, or one of the witnesses is disqualified — even though she shows the conditions between them that he had to add for her — she collects only according to custom (Piskei Maharai siman 89). And see above siman 100 seif 30.} And in all these matters and the like — provincial custom is paramount and they judge accordingly, provided that custom is widespread throughout the province.

{Rama: However, if he wishes to stipulate and reduce for his wife from the custom — the choice is his (Maharil siman 76), provided he does not reduce below what the Sages enacted. And it seems to me specifically when he so stipulated at the time he made the match; but if they made a match without specification and obligated themselves with penalties — he must write according to custom and cannot change (the master's words, and so implied in Maharil). And there are places accustomed to write all ketubot equally even if she brought him nothing; and if he wishes he adds for her; and if he wishes to reduce for her — she writes him "such-and-such I accepted upon my ketubah" — and so is practiced in these countries.}
